avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces CYP3A4, reducing baricitinib plasma concentrations and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative mood support if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May enhance immune activation, potentially counteracting JAK inhibitor immunosuppressive effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under clinical supervision

avoid_supplements.name: Ginseng (American/Asian)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Immune stimulant that may reduce drug efficacy and increase infection risk with JAK inhibitor use
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue use; discuss alternative supplements with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit Extract/Seed
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may slightly increase baricitinib levels
caution_supplements.action: Limit intake; monitor for increased adverse effects if used regularly

caution_supplements.name: Quercetin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition and antiviral properties may affect metabolism
caution_supplements.action: Use in moderation; no dose adjustment typically needed

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Pomelo
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases baricitinib bioavailability and plasma concentration
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit and pomelo; check for hidden sources in juices and supplements

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase baricitinib absorption rate but do not significantly alter overall bioavailability
caution_foods.action: Can be taken with or without food; maintain consistent timing relative to meals

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase hepatotoxicity risk and impair immune function during JAK inhibition
caution_foods.action: Limit to moderate consumption; discuss safe limits with healthcare provider

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of infection, hematologic abnormalities, and lipid/liver enzyme changes. Assess adherence and counsel on immunosuppression risks, particularly with concurrent immune-stimulating supplements that may reduce clinical efficacy.
